title: Typography / Type scale

location.series: IBM Design Language / public web guidelines
location.extent: Complete webpage content-area capture; interactive elements retain their captured state

slide_intent: Coordinate type size and line height while adapting to script and viewing distance, because equal numeric sizes do not always produce equally readable text.
strategic_value: A shared Plex scale with explicit language adjustments can maintain hierarchy across IBM’s global and large-format communications.
demonstration: The page presents a size sequence and formula, default versus adjusted script examples, scale tables, a tester and large-format viewing-distance guidance. The screenshot preserves the visible default table and control states.
practical_value: Choose the appropriate script scale and format multiplier before setting type; consult the preserved source text for table rows or tabs outside the captured state.

content_islands.name: Scale foundation
content_islands.spec: Place the introduction above the increasing Plex size specimen and the formula strip.

content_islands.name: Script adjustment
content_islands.spec: Compare New with Japanese text before and after adjustment, then show paired multilingual examples marked incorrect and correct.

content_islands.name: Universal table and tester
content_islands.spec: Present default size, 95% adjusted size and line-height columns above the captured type tester.

content_islands.name: Viewing distance
content_islands.spec: Explain print and digital scaling beside the diagram of progressively larger planes.

content_islands.name: Large-format table and resources
content_islands.spec: Close with the multiplier tabs and visible table rows, followed by Plex and Carbon resource cards.

ingredient.name: Adjusted Plex type scale
ingredient.role: Preserve legibility and comparable hierarchy across scripts.
ingredient.application: Use the default scale for Latin, Cyrillic, Hebrew and Greek; reduce point size to 95% for Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Devanagari and Arabic while keeping the default line height.
ingredient.scope: The adjustment belongs to the IBM type scale. Separate print and digital multipliers apply to large formats; the source conditions those rules on artwork produced at 100%.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source explains that a shared scale maintains coherence, that script anatomy requires adjustment, and that viewing distance changes apparent size.
reference_purposes.Expression: The increasing Plex specimen and multilingual comparisons demonstrate hierarchy and optical differences.
reference_purposes.Application: The page supplies the scale formula, size/line-height tables and format examples.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Devanagari and Arabic use 95% point size while retaining default line height; large-format rules assume artwork at 100% scale.
